32256-the-big-time.title: The Big Time
32256-the-big-time.creator: Fritz Leiber
32256-the-big-time.description: A book by Fritz Leiber. at sudden death was about to jump you from nowhere? Have you ever been scared of Ghosts--not the story-book kind, but the billions of beings who were once so real and strong it's hard to believe they'll just sleep harmlessly forever?

arxiv-1910-07597.title: 2D Azimuthal Space for Au + Au Mid-Central Collisions at s N ​ N = \sqrt{s_{NN}}= 200 GeV R.S. Longacre a a Brookhaven National Laboratory, Upton, NY 11973, USA
arxiv-1910-07597.description: Abstract In this paper we will show that one can summarize the major two particle reaction plane azimuthal correlations for Au + Au mid-central collisions at s N ​ N = \sqrt{s_{NN}}= 200 GeV by defining a 2D azimuthal space which is a summary of the event by event average.

arxiv-2105-08573.title: Dependent Multi-Task Learning with Causal Intervention for Image Captioning
arxiv-2105-08573.creator: Wenqing Chen, Jidong Tian, Caoyun Fan, Hao He, Yaohui Jin
arxiv-2105-08573.description: Abstract Recent work for image captioning mainly followed an extract-then-generate paradigm, pre-extracting a sequence of object-based features and then formulating image captioning as a single sequence-to-sequence task. Although promising, we observed two problems in generated captions: 1) content inconsistency where models would generate contradicting facts; 2) not informative enough where models would miss parts of important information.

arxiv-2112-06575.title: Gappability Index for Quantum Many-Body Systems
arxiv-2112-06575.creator: Yuan Yao, Masaki Oshikawa, Akira Furusaki
arxiv-2112-06575.description: Abstract We propose an index ℐ G \mathcal{I}_{G} which characterizes the degree of gappability, namely the difficulty to induce a unique ground state with a nonvanishing excitation gap, in the presence of a symmetry G G . ℐ G \mathcal{I}_{G} represents the dimension of the subspace of ambient uniquely-gapped theories in the entire G G -invariant “theory space”.

arxiv-2210-10245.title: A potential system with infinitely many critical periods
arxiv-2210-10245.creator: Jihua Wang
arxiv-2210-10245.description: Abstract . In this paper, we propose an analytical non-polynomial potential system which has infinitely many critical periodic orbits in phase plane. The main approach is Rolle’ Theorem by showing the existence of infinitely many 2 ​ π − 2\pi- periodic solutions, through utilizing variational methods and the properties of Bessel function.

arxiv-2312-06014.title: Linear Quadratic Dual Control
arxiv-2312-06014.creator: Anders Rantzer
arxiv-2312-06014.description: Abstract This is a draft paper originally posted on Arxiv as a documentation of a plenary lecture at CDC2023. The core material has been accepted for publication at L4DC 2024. Certainty equivalence adaptive controllers are analysed using a “data-driven Riccati equation”, corresponding to the model-free Bellman equation used in Q-learning. The equation depends quadratically on data correlation matrices.

arxiv-2402-04867.title: Multimodal Query Suggestion with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback Conference: Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2024; May 13–17, 2024; Singapore Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2024 (WWW’24), May 13–17, 2024, Singapore Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3543507.3583304 ISBN: 9
arxiv-2402-04867.creator: Zheng Wang 1 , Bingzheng Gan 1 , Wei Shi 1
arxiv-2402-04867.description: Abstract . In the rapidly evolving landscape of information retrieval, search engines strive to provide more personalized and relevant results to users. Query suggestion systems play a crucial role in achieving this goal by assisting users in formulating effective queries. However, existing query suggestion systems mainly rely on textual inputs, potentially limiting user search experiences for querying images.

arxiv-2404-00920.title: Farside-dominant quasinuclear rainbow in refractive α \alpha + α \alpha scattering
arxiv-2404-00920.creator: S. Ohkubo
arxiv-2404-00920.description: Abstract α \alpha + α \alpha scattering has a long history since the first experiment by Rutherford and Chadwick in 1927 and has been studied thoroughly experimentally and theoretically. However, α \alpha + α \alpha scattering has never been paid attention from the viewpoint of refractive scattering.

arxiv-2406-15775.title: On well-posedness for parabolic Cauchy problems of Lions type with rough initial data
arxiv-2406-15775.creator: Pascal Auscher, Hedong Hou
arxiv-2406-15775.description: Abstract . We establish a complete picture for well-posedness of parabolic Cauchy problems with time-independent, uniformly elliptic, bounded measurable complex coefficients. We exhibit a range of p p for which tempered distributions in homogeneous Hardy–Sobolev spaces H ˙ s , p {\dot{H}}^{s,p} with regularity index s ∈ ( − 1 , 1 ) s\in(-1,1) are initial data.

arxiv-2410-04277.title: Mechanistic Behavior Editing of Language Models
arxiv-2410-04277.creator: Joykirat Singh, Subhabrata Dutta, Tanmoy Chakraborty
arxiv-2410-04277.description: Abstract Large Language Models trained on web-scale text acquire language generation abilities that can solve a wide range of tasks, particularly when task knowledge is refined into the generative prior using in-context examples. However, spurious features learned from noisy data hinder their generalizability. Supervised finetuning can introduce task specificity, but introduce data inefficiency.

arxiv-2502-02954.title: Direct Distributional Optimization for Provable Alignment of Diffusion Models
arxiv-2502-02954.creator: Ryotaro Kawata, Kazusato Oko, Atsushi Nitanda, Taiji Suzuki
arxiv-2502-02954.description: Abstract We introduce a novel alignment method for diffusion models from distribution optimization perspectives while providing rigorous convergence guarantees. We first formulate the problem as a generic regularized loss minimization over probability distributions and directly optimize the distribution using the Dual Averaging method.

arxiv-2506-02280.title: The State of Large Language Models for African Languages: Progress and Challenges
arxiv-2506-02280.creator: Kedir Yassin Hussen, Walelign Tewabe Sewunetie, Abinew Ali Ayele, Sukairaj Hafiz Imam, Eyob Nigussie Alemu, Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad, Seid Muhie Yimam
arxiv-2506-02280.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are transforming Natural Language Processing (NLP), but their benefits are largely absent for Africa’s 2,000 low-resource languages. This paper comparatively analyzes African language coverage across six LLMs, eight Small Language Models (SLMs), and six Specialized SLMs (SSLMs). The evaluation covers language coverage, training sets, technical limitations, script problems, and language modelling roadmaps.

arxiv-2601-09861.title: Barrier-crossing and energy relaxation dynamics of non-Markovian inertial systems connected via analytical Green-Fokker-Planck approach
arxiv-2601-09861.creator: Roland R. Netz
arxiv-2601-09861.description: Abstract From numerical simulations it is known that the barrier-crossing time of a non-Markovian one-dimensional reaction coordinate with a single exponentially decaying memory function exhibits a memory-turnover: for intermediate values of the memory decay time the barrier-crossing time is reduced compared to the Markovian limit and for long memory times increases quadratically with the memory time when keeping the total

pmc-11541464.title: Do healthy people migrate more? A 21-year follow-up of a rural cohort in Bangladesh
pmc-11541464.creator: Nurul Alam, M Moinuddin Haider, Md Mahabubur Rahman, Mamun Ibn Bashar, Md Tazvir Amin, Katherine S Wander
pmc-11541464.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Demographers have long suspected that health influences whether a person migrates―a “healthy migrant effect” ―but this has rarely been tested for a longer period with high-quality, longitudinal data. This study aimed to assess which measures of health are associated with subsequent migrations among young adults from a rural community in Bangladesh, adjusted for socio-demographic characteristics, and how long these associations persist.

pmc-12557969.title: Academic misconduct and artificial intelligence use by medical students, interns and PhD students in Ukraine: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12557969.creator: Lesya Lymar, Iurii Kuchyn, Kateryna Bielka, Livia Puljak
pmc-12557969.description: BackgroundThe issues regarding the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and academic integrity are important contemporary topics. There are no clear regulations governing the use of AI in academic institutions in Ukraine. This study aimed to explore the perceptions of medical students, interns, and PhD candidates about academic misconduct and AI use.

pmc-12608465.title: Experimental and DEM Study on the Mechanical Behaviors of Sand–Fines Mixtures with Different Fines Contents and Particle Size Ratios
pmc-12608465.creator: Kejia Wu, Bing Lv, Hexige Baoyin, Dongsheng Li, Zhouyi Yan, Pengqiang Yu, Yang Liu, Antonio Caggiano
pmc-12608465.description: To clarify the regulatory laws of the fines content (FC) and particle size ratio (SR) on the mechanical properties of sand–fines mixtures and reveal the underlying microscopic mechanical mechanisms, this study takes sand–fines mixtures composed of natural river sand and silt as the research object.

pmc-13317052.title: Prognostic Value of Cardiac Biomarkers in Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13317052.creator: Jaisingh Rajput, Indresh Yadav, Bryan O Oyarebu, Usman G Lashari, Ahmad Mohammad, Mandeep Kaur, Shelly Ibadin, Evangelos A Kolotouros
pmc-13317052.description: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, necessitating effective risk stratification to improve clinical outcomes. Biomarkers, including cardiac troponins, natriuretic peptides, inflammatory markers, and more recently neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), galectin-3 (Gal-3), and microRNAs (miR-208b and miR-499), have been investigated for their prognostic potential.

pmc-13343336.title: Provider perceptions of an antimicrobial stewardship program in immunocompromised patients at a cancer center
pmc-13343336.creator: Raneem H. Pallotta, Julia E. Szymczak, Emily S. Spivak, Hannah Imlay
pmc-13343336.description: Although provider opposition has been identified as a barrier to initiating antimicrobial stewardship programs (ASPs) among immunocompromised (IC) patients, little is known about perceptions of IC ASPs postimplementation. We assessed provider perceptions of our cancer hospital-focused ASP. Respondents found the ASP to be acceptable and value-added.

pmc-13398325.title: Influence of X-Chromosome Inactivation in Pathogenesis of Turner Syndrome
pmc-13398325.creator: Ana-Maria Grigore, Lavinia Caba, Vlad Teodor Iacob, Lucian-Mihai Antoci, Monica Cristina Pânzaru, Lăcrămioara Ionela Butnariu, Eusebiu Vlad Gorduza
pmc-13398325.description: Turner syndrome (TS), a disorder caused by the complete or partial absence of an X chromosome, exhibits significant clinical variability that cannot be fully explained by chromosomal anomalies alone. This narrative review highlights the crucial role of epigenetic mechanisms, particularly X-chromosome inactivation (XCI), in shaping the TS phenotype.

pmc-13411680.title: Comparison of Functional and Hemodynamic Parameters Between Methamphetamine-Associated and Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13411680.creator: Fani Papaioannou, Thomas Karagiannis, Afroditi Boutou, Athina Georgopoulou, Stergios Kaprinis, Georgia Pitsiou
pmc-13411680.description: Background: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare functional and hemodynamic parameters between patients with Meth-APAH and idiopathic PAH (IPAH). Methods: MEDLINE, Scopus, and gray literature were searched up to September 2025. Eligible studies were observational and compared functional and hemodynamic parameters between patients with Meth-APAH and IPAH.
